title: Biographical identification
description: Charm Barnard states her name, birth details Seattle September 8 1945, marital status, maiden name Stotsenberg, and lack of nicknames.

title: Migration to Idaho; family residences
description: She describes moving to Nez Perce Idaho in fourth grade from Aberdeen, traveling by car, and notes her mother's earlier covered wagon journey.

title: Parents and siblings
description: Barnard provides details about her mother Dorothy Knight's boarding house work and her father John's ministry and United Good Neighbors executive role, their divorce, and her sister Jill and deceased brothers.

title: Husband and marriage; education
description: She identifies husband Michael, born December 29 1945 in Amarillo Texas, their marriage July 8 1967 in McMinville Oregon, and her attendance at Portland State, Santa Monica City College, and Lewis & Clark.

title: Skills and occupations; hobbies
description: Barnard lists practical skills including toilet repair and needlework, employment as switchboard operator receptionist newspaper worker property manager and VISTA volunteer, and interests in art pottery weaving gardening and photography.

title: Awards; rural living comparisons
description: She mentions flower arranging prizes at the Lewiston Fair, then compares benefits of small-town nature access and community against narrow-mindedness and limited recreation.

title: Childhood freedom; sibling rivalry
description: Barnard describes childhood freedom contrasted with current financial independence, details fights with sister Jill over paper dolls and parental affection, and notes college was not expected.

title: Courtship and marriage; recreation
description: She recounts meeting Michael at a Los Angeles newspaper their intellectual courtship nine months of dating, and current dancing movies and yoga recreation habits.

title: Financial support; community activism
description: Barnard discusses her switchboard work current VISTA position major financial responsibility for two years, organizing the Women's Center crisis center and bookstore, and advice for women moving to small towns.

title: Media consumption; move to Lewiston
description: She reads Ms. magazine and donated magazines but cannot afford subscriptions, rarely watches TV, explains family ties and Michael's hepatitis brought them to Lewiston from Mexico, and describes marital conversations.

title: Closing reflections on small-town life
description: Barnard reflects that Lewiston's small size means visibility in women's movement work but requires careful behavior monitoring.
